analysis.title: Zealand Pharma A/S (ZELA.CO) 3Q26 review: glepaglutide EU approval the near-term catalyst; obesity newsflow quieter for now
key_insights: GS keeps Buy on Zealand Pharma (ZELA.CO) and cuts the 12m price target to DKK 418 from DKK 452 (-8%). Price is Dkr245.10, implying 70.5% upside. The cut reflects lower FY27-35 revenue/EPS estimates (c.12%/27% lower on average) and a six-month DCF roll-forward.

3Q26 was uneventful for the equity story. FY26 operating expense guidance narrowed to DKK 2,700-3,000mn from DKK 2,700-3,300mn, with the midpoint about 5% lower than before. FY26 collaboration revenue guidance was maintained at c.DKK 4.5bn.

The near-term catalyst is European approval of glepaglutide (GLP-2 analog) for short bowel syndrome (SBS) after a positive CHMP opinion. The catalyst calendar shows an EMA decision in 4Q26. GS says approval could remove a gating factor ahead of Phase 3 data for US approval (EASE-5 is still recruiting).

Management is targeting a commercialization partnership for glepaglutide and reports significant partner interest. It sees the existing SBS market at >$1bn, with potential to expand given twice-weekly dosing. GS views glepaglutide as differentiated versus standard of care and the opportunity as underappreciated.

Balance sheet: cash of DKK 13.5bn (c.$2.0bn). Zealand completed its $200mn share buyback. A net cash inflow of $400mn from Roche is expected in 4Q26 ($575mn Phase 3 milestone less a $175mn combination contribution payment).

Obesity pipeline is the key investor focus and the basis for GS's positive view, but newsflow is quieter. Petrelintide monotherapy Phase 3 (ZUPREME-3, -4, -5) has started with Roche. The Phase 2 ZYNERGY combination of petrelintide with CT-388 is on track to start in 4Q26. Management gave no weight loss target or timing for ZYNERGY data.

Partner Boehringer Ingelheim plans global regulatory submissions for survodutide in 2027 and is adding a Phase 3 trial in type 2 diabetes plus three Phase 3b studies (SYNCHRONIZE-START, SYNCHRONIZE-HERA, ELEVATE-LIVER) with more flexible dose escalation. The LIVERAGE Phase 3 interim analysis in MASH is expected in 2027. Management sees MASH data as an added reason to prescribe survodutide in obesity.

Petrelintide differentiation may extend beyond weight loss to bone mass preservation. Weight loss stepped down from 10.7% in ZUPREME-1 to 9.2% at an earlier 28-week timepoint in ZUPREME-2. Management attributes this partly to amylins not being insulin secreting, and says confirmation is needed in Phase 3 T2D and non-T2D populations. Management positions the monotherapy around double-digit weight loss with placebo-like tolerability, and the combination for patients needing greater weight loss.
For ZP9830, management is interested in an early partnership after Phase 1b psoriasis data.

3Q26 vs estimates: revenue DKK 4mn, 18-20% below GSe (DKK 5mn) and 97% below Visible Alpha consensus (DKK 147mn). Total opex DKK 689mn, 19% below GSe (DKK 855mn) and 6% below VA (DKK 736mn). EBIT excluding other operating income was DKK -685mn versus GSe DKK -850mn. Reported EBIT of DKK -54mn includes DKK 631mn of other operating income tied to the rusfertide royalty agreement. EPS (basic) was DKK -0.79 versus GSe -9.26 and VA -8.69.

Model changes: FY26 EBIT/EPS estimates rise c.66%/51% on lower cost assumptions. GS removes Zegalogue royalties, adjusts milestone payments and updates FX. GS FY26E EPS is DKK 29.40 (old 19.41), FY27E 4.79 (old 9.94), FY28E -58.97 (old -41.03). FY26E revenue is DKK 4,529mn, FY27E 5,280mn and FY28E 886mn.
Valuation is a DCF with 12% WACC and 0% terminal growth. M&A rank is 3, which does not factor into the price target. Shares are down 26.9% over 3m, 29.3% over 6m and 48.3% over 12m.

market_movers.rationale: Buy kept with the 12m target cut to DKK 418 from DKK 452 on lower FY27-35 estimates and the DCF roll-forward. Obesity pipeline and glepaglutide EU approval underpin the view. Zealand's primary listing is in Copenhagen with no US ticker confirmed in the report.

sector_views.rationale: Buy rating on Zealand relative to its coverage universe. The obesity pipeline (petrelintide, survodutide) is the basis for the positive view.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 reported revenue DKK 4mn versus GSe DKK 5mn and Visible Alpha consensus DKK 147mn (consensus est.).
3Q26 total opex DKK 689mn reported versus GSe DKK 855mn and VA DKK 736mn (estimates).

3Q26 reported EBIT DKK -54mn includes DKK 631mn of other operating income from the rusfertide royalty agreement. EBIT excluding that item was DKK -685mn versus GSe DKK -850mn and VA DKK -813mn (estimates).
3Q26 reported basic EPS DKK -0.79 versus GSe DKK -9.26 and VA DKK -8.69 (estimates). 3Q25 was DKK -5.75.
FY26 opex guidance narrowed to DKK 2,700-3,000mn (midpoint 2,850) from DKK 2,700-3,300mn. GSe DKK 2,903mn and VA DKK 2,930mn (pre-earnings consensus) are 2%/3% above the new midpoint.
FY26 collaboration revenue guidance maintained at c.DKK 4,500mn. GSe DKK 4,543mn and VA DKK 4,719mn are 1%/5% above guidance.
Cash of DKK 13.5bn at quarter end, in line with GSe. A net $400mn inflow from Roche is expected in 4Q26.
risk_factors: Stronger-than-expected clinical data from obesity market competitors.
Clinical failures of pipeline assets including glepaglutide, survodutide and petrelintide.
Petrelintide weight loss stepped down to 9.2% at 28 weeks in ZUPREME-2 from 10.7% in ZUPREME-1. Phase 3 confirmation is still needed.

tension_points.bull_case: Petrelintide Phase 3 has started with Roche, survodutide submissions are planned for 2027, and the combination could serve patients needing the greatest weight loss. GS Buy with a DKK 418 target.
tension_points.bear_case: Petrelintide weight loss stepped down to 9.2% at 28 weeks in ZUPREME-2 from 10.7% in ZUPREME-1, and the report says confirmation is required in Phase 3. Stronger competitor data and a tougher payer environment are listed risks.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Phase 3 T2D and non-T2D data that fail to confirm the weight loss seen in ZUPREME-2.
